settings.subtitle.rules.label: Subtitle rules
settings.subtitle.rules.hint: Subtitle markers are read line by line on import: a line of only brackets is SFX, brackets at the start of a dialogue line name that line's speaker, and brackets mid-line are only removed from the text, never taken as a name. A speaker is recorded only if every dialogue line in a subtitle entry is labeled; if any line isn't, none is (better too few than wrong). If a brackets-only line is directly followed by an unlabeled dialogue line, neither the SFX nor the speaker is accepted. Subtitle styles vary, so it's best to clean them first into one person per entry with every line labeled. Applies only to markers imported later; existing lines can be re-read with the current rules using "Regenerate speakers"
settings.subtitle.sfx_rule.label: SFX lines
settings.subtitle.sfx_rule.hint: A full-line match → this line is SFX (unless the next line is unlabeled dialogue: then it may be a name on its own line, and neither is accepted). Default: a line made up only of one or more complete brackets (full-width or half-width, may nest or repeat; line breaks inside brackets don't count)
settings.subtitle.note_rule.label: Note brackets
settings.subtitle.note_rule.hint: Note sections within a line (named group content). Alignment text and names drop them; an SFX line's name is built from their content. Default: all outermost brackets, may nest
settings.subtitle.speaker_rule.label: Speaker label
settings.subtitle.speaker_rule.hint: Matched only at the start of a dialogue line (several in a row are fine); named group name is that line's speaker. Brackets mid-line are never names. Default: complete brackets at line start
settings.subtitle.speaker_split.label: Speaker name split (optional)
settings.subtitle.speaker_split.hint: Splits one label into several names with this regex (several people speaking at once). Default: 、. Empty = no split
settings.subtitle.speaker_clean.label: Speaker name cleanup (optional)
settings.subtitle.speaker_clean.hint: Removes matching parts from names (such as nested readings). Empty = no cleanup

studio.getSay: Vocal separation is done by PyMSS Studio, installed separately (free software, AGPL-3.0, not bundled with this app). Download the installer for your platform from its release page (macOS: the MLX build for Apple Silicon; Windows: the CUDA / CPU / ROCm build for your graphics card). Once installed, finish the environment setup in Studio, download separation models (such as bs_roformer_voc_hyperacev2, becruily_deux), then come back here and refresh.

transcript.help: Click a line = set the selection to it and jump to its start (no playback). Shift+click = extend the selection to it. Double-click = play it. Right-click = its menu (create sample, speech analysis, edit…). No following for 3.5 s after manual scrolling. ✎ = edited, ◆ = phoneme times fixed by hand, ? = original subtitles had labels but no speaker was recorded. The search box above searches this episode's lines (text or reading): Enter for next, Shift+Enter for previous, Esc to clear. ⌘⇧F or / in the script focuses it.
transcript.opedNote: {n} lines · skipped in batch sampling and batch analysis
transcript.notImported: Not imported to the text layer yet

import.footer: Reads in the background; no copying, no transcoding

import.groupsInfer: After import, grouped by file name: {list}.

workType.note: Only checked items change. Work sets the grouping on the Sources page; work and type pass live to samples on these sources (work: / type: tags). Can be undone.
workType.done: Changed work and type on {n} sources
speech.scope.source: Scope: lines outside OP/ED on the selected sources (no samples needed first), on the chosen track
speech.scope.samples: Scope: lines in the judge range of the selected samples, on the default vocal track (otherwise the sample's own track or the first vocal track above it covering the whole line, otherwise the original mix)
speech.scope.units: Scope: checked lines (each on the track it was last measured on)
speech.say: Phonemes belong to the source timeline: a line has one copy, read by every track on the source (original mix, separated stems, flattened results…); the track it was measured on is only recorded. Re-imported results have their own copy. Measured only on vocal tracks covering the whole line. Only this line's text is sent; the window = the line's range plus the alignment tolerance on each side (Settings: Speech analysis).
speech.blocked.no-text: No lines in the judge range
speech.blocked.out-of-track: This line is outside this track's range
speech.blocked.no-voice: This track has no vocal (not marked as a vocal track)
speech.blocked.partial-track: This track covers only part of this line (speech analysis needs the whole line)
speech.mixBound: Lines in scope on the original mix or a track with no role: {n}. To analyze the vocal instead, separate the full track first, then set the default vocal track.
speech.envOk: Environment: model files in place (this only means the files exist, not that inference has been tested; you can test it in Settings "Environment and models")
speech.envMissing: Missing model files: {models}. The job will fail. Put them in place first, using the paths in Settings "Environment and models".
speech.envNoF0: Missing {model}: alignment runs as usual, but pitch (F0) is not measured this time, and the job will note this when it finishes. Features that use pitch (pitch search, pitch and energy in rhythm, etc.) have no data at these positions for now. You can download it or import it from a file in Settings → Environment and models.
speech.queued: Queued analysis ({n}) · see per-item results in the job when it finishes
speech.results.rerun: Run speech analysis again on checked
error.speech-f0-failed: Pitch (F0) failed for {failed} / {total} segments (60 s each). Alignment results are kept as usual. Features that use pitch (pitch search, pitch and energy in rhythm, etc.) have no data at these positions for now. Cause: {cause}
speech.layer.label: Overlay
speech.noVoice: This track is not marked as a vocal track (it is marked SFX only, or is a separated stem with no role), so phonemes are not read and speech analysis can't run on it. If needed, turn on "Vocal" for it in "Tracks and roles".
speech.noText.no-text: No lines in the judge range (normal for a manual clip). You can play, clip, flatten the whole sample or export right away. For rhythm features or "Vowels only" flatten, provide the line as actually spoken (this adds a line over the judge range):
speech.provideLabel: Enter the line as actually spoken
speech.editing: Editing: phoneme timing (saved as a manual version)
speech.editHint: Drag a boundary to change timing. Shared boundaries move together and can't cross a neighbor. Esc to discard.
speech.manualSaved: Saved as a manual version (later automatic analysis won't overwrite it)
speech.timesNote: Each line: start seconds Tab end seconds Tab phoneme. Only times can change; line count, labels and order can't.
speech.partial: ◐ Reads only part of a line (the sample range doesn't cover all of it)
speech.conflict: Unavailable: line {a} and line {b} overlap at {start}–{end} s. Shrink the judge range, or fix the phoneme timing of one of them.
speech.unit.reads: Lines this sample reads in the judge range: {n}.
speech.unit.shared: Editing phoneme timing, switching versions or editing text changes this line's single copy. It applies at once to samples reading this line on all tracks of the source and to the phoneme layer on the Sources page (re-imported outputs have their own copy).
speech.unit.measuredOn: Phonemes for this line were measured on "{track}".

roots.groupWhole: Create full-length samples for all {n} in group…

flatten.title: Flatten bench
flatten.sub: Audio: {track} · outer selection [{a}, {b}) s (fixed on open)
flatten.defaultsNote: Defaults depend on the entry point. Details: from first vowel + edge left. Other single entries: whole + auto in segment. Batch: vowels only + auto in segment (changeable in Settings). Changing the range doesn't change the target pitch.
flatten.modelsMissing: Missing model files: {models}. The job will fail (it won't switch to another device or method).
flatten.ownPlayer: Own audition here, stops on close
flatten.est.cached: Cached estimate; the actual input measured at run time takes precedence
flatten.est.cachedOnly: Estimated from cache; the actual input measured at run time takes precedence
flatten.est.inJob: Estimate: no pitch measurement for this sound yet, so it is determined during the job (the actual input measured at run time takes precedence)
flatten.innerHint: Drag a gold inner range on the waveform. Outside it, audio is kept as is. Within the transitions on each side, pitch moves smoothly from the original to the target. The plateau without transitions must be at least 30 ms.
flatten.needAlignment: This range needs a speech analysis result covering the outer selection (same sound). If there is none, run speech analysis first, or use whole / inner flatten.
flatten.manualAlignment: Alignment is a manually corrected version: vowel ranges are not tightened by energy
flatten.name: Name
flatten.productNote: The name has no note name; pitch goes in the pitch: tag. The output is a pitched one-shot sample that inherits the original's character. A failure registers nothing. When done it only shows "Data updated" and doesn't switch the current sample.
flatten.range.whole.note: Resynthesizes the whole outer selection, with no fades at the ends
flatten.range.vowels.note: Resynthesizes each vowel / N separately; consonants and silence between them stay sample-identical. Needs alignment.
flatten.range.first.note: Keeps everything before the first vowel as is; voiced parts after it use one target. Needs alignment.
flatten.range.inner.note: Drag a gold inner range on the waveform. Transitions default to 0.05 s on each side.
flatten.target.auto.note: Confidence-weighted median of reliable frames in the processed range, snapped to the nearest semitone
flatten.target.edge.note: 100 ms inward from the chosen edge. Reports an error if evidence is insufficient; doesn't switch sides.
flatten.target.manual.note: Note name (A4, C#5, B♭3) or frequency with unit (445Hz, no snapping)
flatten.queued: Flatten queued · when done it only shows "Data updated" and doesn't switch the current sample
flatten.batchSub: Each item gets its own target from its own range and edges
flatten.batchBody: Samples: {n}. Each produces a "pitched one-shot" output, registered directly (with a pitch: tag). Items without alignment fail individually, with a reason, under a range that needs it. The current list and selection stay unchanged. Results are listed per item in the Jobs drawer, and you can rerun only the failed ones.
flatten.batchAutoOnly: Batch only offers auto targets (each item uses its own pitch), with no manual note name or inner flatten
handoff.head: Whole sample · {name}

handoff.reaperN: Original audio, beat-fitted by stretch markers ({n}, in sequence)

reaper.copiedN: Copied ({n}, in sequence, one bar apart) · in REAPER, select a track and cursor position, then paste
library.auditionBoth: Audition: left click original, right click beat-fit · ⌥ drag out original, ⌥⇧ drag out beat-fit, ⌥⌘ drag into REAPER (with stretch markers)
top.bpm.tip: Global target BPM (20–400). Empty: beat-fit at the original speech rate. With a BPM: by default uses the nearest binary plan no slower than the original.
top.bpm.changed: BPM {bpm} · audition stopped, beat-fit plan recalculated as needed
rhythm.none: No rhythm analysis for this sample yet. You can still play, clip, flatten or export it. For beat-fit, run speech analysis first.
rhythm.manualStale: Manual splits / cells / cuts belong to an older analysis version and are not applied now.
rhythm.moraSaved: Mora cells written to manual cells (can undo)
rhythm.mapLabel: Time mapping between the original line and beat-fit
rhythm.mapCaption: Original {a} s → beat-fit {b} s · same-scale time axis · onset core kept sample for sample
rhythm.cellAuto: Reset to auto (inferred from original rhythm)
rhythm.cellsNote: Changes save immediately (can undo) and only rebuild derived rhythm. Applies to this sample only.
rhythm.attrsNote: Relative pitch / loudness use the pause group as baseline. Pitch uses reliable frames only. Unmeasured values show "Unknown".
rhythm.splitNote: Click a vowel or moraic nasal to split before it (for when a repeated vowel is actually voiced again); click again to cancel. Changing split points also clears manual cells and cuts.
rhythm.cutNote: Click a block to cut before it. Click an auto cut (pause ≥ threshold) to merge.
rhythm.cutNone: Block {n}: click to cut before it
rhythm.cutAuto: Before block {n}: auto cut (click to merge)
rhythm.cutMerged: Before block {n}: auto cut merged (click to restore)
rhythm.cutManual: Before block {n}: manual cut (click to cancel)
settings.analysis.penalty.label: Large-number penalty
settings.analysis.penalty.hint: 1× is the original weight 0.045. Affects only cell inference for "original rhythm · no mora". Changing it only rebuilds derived rhythm, with no re-inference.
settings.analysis.pause_sensitivity.hint: Default for new samples (0.5–2). Each sample can change it under "Grouping and pauses" in the speech panel. Changing this doesn't affect existing samples.
settings.analysis.segment_threshold.hint: Pauses at least this long split a sentence into phrases (default for new samples, 0.16–2 s). Changing this doesn't affect existing samples.
settings.export.reaper_snap.label: REAPER handoff snap
settings.export.reaper_snap.hint: When pasting into REAPER: the first onset lands on the edit cursor (onset consonants stay before the cursor), or the item start does.
handoff.reaperBaked: Copy REAPER handoff (beat-fitted audio, markers only for fine-tuning)
settings.export.reaper_kind.label: REAPER handoff copied by ⌘C
settings.export.reaper_kind.hint: In the Library, ⌘C (outside text fields) copies the checked samples, or the current sample if none are checked. The menu has both kinds.
settings.export.reaper_kind.unbaked: Original audio, beat-fitted by stretch markers
settings.export.video_codec.label: Video clip codec
settings.export.video_codec.hint: Default is H.264 MP4 + AAC (works directly in most software). The high-quality intermediate codec is ProRes 422 HQ MOV + 24-bit PCM (large files, suited to further work in AE and the like).
storage.title: Storage
storage.hint: Only regenerable caches and intermediate files from successful separation jobs can be cleaned. Tracks in the library folder, independent files, exports, measurements (including the pitch search index) and the database are never treated as cache. Files created or changed in the last 15 minutes are protected.
storage.cat.cache.hint: Waveform peaks, thumbnails, frame indexes, beat-fit preview renders, Studio model list, leftover temp files
storage.cat.searchIndex: Speech search index and one-shot metrics
storage.cat.searchIndex.hint: Derived data in the database; rebuilt in the background if deleted
storage.cat.measurements.hint: Measurements are not cache and are not cleaned
storage.cat.backups.hint: Data/Backups/: needed to go back to the previous version; the latest is always kept
storage.unusedHint: Extra tracks from repeated separation, or outputs left after deleting samples. Default tracks aren't listed.
storage.unusedLeft: Files in use, not deleted for now: {n}.
storage.unusedConfirmBody: Deletes the files too, {size} in total. This can't be undone. Speech analysis on these tracks ({n}) is deleted with them.
storage.cat.exports.hint: Library folder Exports/ and REAPER/: DAW projects may reference them, so they are never deleted automatically
storage.cat.jobs.hint: Job inputs and logs. Intermediate files from successful separation jobs can be cleaned (new jobs delete them on success); failed jobs keep them as evidence.
storage.derived: Also clear the speech search index and one-shot metrics (rebuilt later in the background)
storage.never.note: Manual cleanup is unavailable while jobs are queued or running. Renaming, moving or replacing files in the library folder breaks references; handle it in the app (relocate / re-import).

shortcuts.reaper: Copy REAPER handoff (kind set in Settings "Export")

shortcuts.waveMark: Waveform: set current position as selection start / end
shortcuts.waveStep: Waveform: move one frame · 1 ms · 5 s
search.running: Searching… (can be canceled; doesn't block other actions)
search.done: Samples: {n} · hits: {m} · pinned result (later background changes won't reorder it)
search.closeResult: Close (removes the result set only, not the samples)
search.status: Pinned result · samples: {n} · hits: {m} · {ms} ms · without valid analysis: {k}

search.noneReady: No searchable samples in the current scope: prepare the index first
search.speech.edge.head: From start
search.speech.noBpm: No BPM: compares normalized rhythm shape
search.speech.bounds: Blocks must be inside the query range, with positive length and no overlap
search.speech.tooClose: Onsets of adjacent blocks must be more than twice the tolerance apart
search.speech.pick: Select a block to edit its conditions here
search.speech.sustain: Sound must last to block end
search.speech.hintFree: "+ Block" adds a block · drag to reorder · Delete to remove
search.speech.hintRoll: Drag empty space to draw a block · drag a block to move it · drag its right edge to resize · Delete to remove
search.speech.speedPref: Original-speed preference (0 = rank by rhythm only)
search.pitch.ignoreOctaveHint: Shifting the whole query by some octaves (the same shift for every block) still counts as a hit; the hit shows "Octave +1"
search.pitch.head: Start tolerance (s)
search.pitch.pick: Select a block, or click empty space to add one
search.pitch.fix: The query has problems. Fix them before searching.
search.pitch.problem.too-short: Blocks must be at least {min} s
search.pitch.problem.range-inverted: Range is inverted (low must not be above high)
search.pitch.problem.bad-note: Invalid note name (e.g. A4, C♯5, B♭3)
search.pitch.problem.bad-line: Can't read this line (each line: seconds pitch, or seconds low..high, or seconds from->to)
search.pitch.hint: Click empty space: add block at end · drag up/down: change pitch · drag right edge: change duration (≥0.1 s, total ≤10 s) · ↑/↓ semitone · Delete to remove
search.pitch.cannotCopy: The query has problems and can't be copied
search.metrics.note: Filters the current scope instantly. Items missing a chosen metric don't match.
search.metrics.prepare: Prepare metrics for current scope in background
search.metrics.queued: Queued: prepare metrics for current scope
search.row.deletedKeep: This sample was deleted; the search record is kept for reference
search.row.stale: Hit no longer valid (analysis or measurements changed). Search again.
search.row.invalid: Hit no longer valid. Search again.
search.row.sourceHits: Source track · click a hit to jump to the source
search.hit.play: Left click: original · right click: beat-fit (with the plan chosen by this hit's evidence)
search.hit.playPitch: Left click: original (pitch hits have no beat-fit)
metric.effectiveDuration.def: First to last frame where the envelope (5 ms RMS) is ≥ 1% of peak
metric.attackTime.def: Envelope first reaches 10% of peak → first reaches 90% (before the peak)
metric.decayTime.def: After the peak, first drops below 90% → first drops below 10%
metric.crestDb.def: Peak sample ÷ RMS in the effective range, in dB; higher means sharper
metric.rmsDb.def: RMS level of the effective range (scaling everything by ×0.1 lowers it by 20 dB)
metric.lowRatio.def: Energy at 20–200 Hz ÷ total energy above 20 Hz
metric.midRatio.def: Energy at 200–4000 Hz ÷ total energy above 20 Hz
metric.highRatio.def: Energy above 4000 Hz ÷ total energy above 20 Hz
metric.centroid.def: Energy-weighted average frequency; higher is brighter
metric.flatness.def: Spectral flatness = geometric mean ÷ arithmetic mean; closer to 1 is more noise-like
metric.pitch.def: Median MIDI of reliable frames in the sample's own F0 measurement (A4 = 69)
metric.pitchSpread.def: P90 − P10 of MIDI across reliable frames
metric.harmonicRatio.def: Energy near harmonics on reliable F0 frames ÷ total energy
metric.highHarmonicRatio.def: Energy of 5th and higher harmonics ÷ all harmonic energy
metric.attackLowRatio.def: Share of energy at 20–200 Hz in the attack
metric.attackHighRatio.def: Share of energy above 4000 Hz in the attack
metric.bodyLowRatio.def: Share of energy at 20–200 Hz in the body
metric.bodyHighRatio.def: Share of energy above 4000 Hz in the body
metric.tailLowRatio.def: Share of energy at 20–200 Hz in the tail
metric.tailHighRatio.def: Share of energy above 4000 Hz in the tail
settings.analysis.auto_prepare.label: Prepare search automatically
settings.analysis.auto_prepare.hint: Runs in the background: measures pitch (F0) for new samples and each source's default vocal track (original mix if none), and builds the speech search index after speech analysis. Queued behind jobs you submit. Takes little space (F0 about 4 MB per hour of audio, speech search index about 1.6 KB per entry). When off, use "Prepare" in the search popover.
layers.help: Shift-click selects a whole segment, Shift-drag snaps to overlapping edges. Double-click a lane to switch to the overlay. Right-click a line or hint to create a sample
seg.menu.head: Line "{text}"
seg.regenerated: Regenerated speakers for {n} lines (edited lines and hand-set speakers left alone)
seg.regeneratedMany: Regenerated speakers for {n} lines across {m} sources (edited lines and hand-set speakers left alone)
hint.menu.head: SFX hint "{text}"
seg.note: A line is what was said (used by speech analysis). After you change its text or edges, its existing analysis stops being used right away (samples reading it show "Needs re-analysis") and it must be analyzed again. Changing only the speakers doesn't affect analysis. Existing samples don't move and keep their names.
seg.usedBy: Used by {n} samples; changes will affect them
seg.flag.edited: ✎ Edited (not replaced when subtitles are imported again)
seg.withheld: ? The subtitles have labels, but who said each line can't be determined, so no speaker was recorded
seg.cut: Cut (shrink old lines to outside the new one)
seg.cutUnavailable: Cut works only when each overlapping line reaches in from one side. If the new line sits inside an old one or covers it entirely, you can only replace or cancel
seg.deletedUsed: Line deleted; the {n} samples reading it can no longer read it
seg.merged: Merged into one line (old analysis no longer used; needs re-analysis)
hint.note: SFX hints are for picking by hand: they apply to the whole source, show on all tracks, aren't aligned, and carry no tags. Hints you added or edited aren't replaced when subtitles are imported again.
newsamples.note.segments: Each line creates a separate sample, extended {a} / {b} s before / after (change in Settings), on "{track}". Name = line text, nature = speech, judge range = line. Can be repeated. Lines in OP/ED are skipped
newsamples.note.hints: Each hint creates a separate sample, extended {a} / {b} s before / after (change in Settings), on "{track}". Name = text in brackets, nature = unpitched one-shot, judge range = hint. Can be repeated. Hints in OP/ED are skipped
newsamples.subMany: {n} selected sources, each on its own default track
newsamples.noteMany.segments: Each line creates a separate sample, extended {a} / {b} s before / after (change in Settings), on each source's default vocal track. Name = line text, nature = speech, judge range = line. Lines in OP/ED are skipped
newsamples.noteMany.hints: Each hint creates a separate sample, extended {a} / {b} s before / after (change in Settings), on each source's default SFX track. Name = hint text. Hints in OP/ED are skipped
newsamples.missingMany.vocal: {n} sources have lines but no default vocal track and aren't listed. Set their default tracks first (no fallback to the original mix).
newsamples.missingMany.sfx: {n} sources have SFX hints but no default SFX track and aren't listed. Set their default tracks first (no fallback to the original mix).
newsamples.noteNoTrack: Set a default track first (no fallback to the original mix)
newsamples.noteWhole: Each source gets one whole-length sample on its analysis track, named after the file. Always creates new ones (repeating makes duplicates)
newsamples.emptyBody.segments: First use "Import subtitles…", or right-click a selection on the Sources page and choose "Add line…"
newsamples.emptyBody.hints: SFX rows go into the SFX hint layer when subtitles are imported. You can also right-click a selection on the Sources page and choose "Add SFX hint…"
newsamples.emptyBody.whole: None of the selected sources has a usable track
newsamples.stale: Default track, role, OP/ED, extension settings, or text layer changed since the preview. Previewed again; please confirm once more
subclear.title: Delete imported subtitle markers on {n} sources
subclear.plan: Imported from subtitles: {segments} lines, {hints} SFX hints, {oped} OP/ED.
subclear.analyzed: {n} lines have speech analysis; it stops being used once they are deleted.
subclear.usedBy: {n} samples read these lines. The samples stay but no longer read them (original line and speaker tags will change).
subclear.protected: Also delete edited lines and those with hand-corrected phonemes ({n}, kept by default)
subclear.note: Lines typed by hand ({typed}) aren't touched. Deleting is one edit and can be undone. You can import subtitles again from scratch afterward.
subimport.quickDoneOpedError: Imported {segments} lines, {hints} SFX hints; OP/ED markers have problems and weren't registered
subimport.stat.replace: Replace (deletes {removed} existing; {analyzed} lines have analysis and need re-analysis)
subimport.stat.skip: Skip (touches a protected line, or Keep existing is chosen)
subimport.removedProtected: Will delete {n} protected existing items (edited or with hand-corrected phoneme versions), along with those edits and corrections
subimport.speakersOff: Speakers not imported (lines carry no speaker)
subimport.opedErrorsHead: OP/ED markers have problems and weren't registered automatically. They are registered with the import only after you confirm each pair's use:
subimport.noPairs: No OP/ED markers in the subtitles
subimport.forceBody: This row touches {n} protected existing items. Force replace deletes them, along with the edits and corrections below (the whole import can be undone):
subimport.forceKeeps: Existing samples don't move and keep their names. Samples reading these lines will need re-analysis
sources.deleteTextLayer: {n} lines, {h} SFX hints, {g} range tags, {o} OP/ED ranges
judge.label: Judge range
judge.needSel: Select a region on the waveform first (must be within the sample)
judge.note: Decides which range tags are inherited and which lines' analysis is read. Must be within the sample
speech.addLineNeedsSel: Select a region on the waveform first
speech.notCurrentHead: This line's current version doesn't match its present content, so the matching version is used here. To fix phoneme timing, switch to it under "Version" first
speech.unit.label: Line {n} · {name}
speech.blocked.rhythm-segments-missing: Unavailable: line {segments} read here isn't analyzed yet. Click "Speech analysis…" to analyze.
speech.blocked.rhythm-segment-stale: Unavailable: line {segments} was edited and needs re-analysis (old analysis no longer used).
speech.trackDefault: Default vocal track (original mix if none)
speech.scope.segments: Scope: these lines, on the selected track
settings.analysis.auto_rerun_segments.la: Re-analyze edited lines in the background
settings.analysis.auto_rerun_segments.hi: After you change a line's text or edges (including split, merge, and cut), queues a background job to analyze it again on the tracks it was analyzed on. When off (default), the old analysis stops being used right away, samples reading it show "Needs re-analysis", and you re-run it by hand. Not triggered when importing subtitles replaces lines.
speech.clipped: ◐ Partly cut off by the sample range
scope.label: Scope
scope.presetHead: Scope presets (saved filters) · choosing one replaces the current scope
scope.addExpr: Tag expression… (tags only; separate from the find bar's expression, saved in the filter)
scope.onlyTags: Filters hold tags only. Text and stars belong in the find bar above and aren't saved in filters
scope.saveSay: Saves the {n} tag conditions in the scope row (find bar text, expressions, and stars aren't saved).
scope.manageSub: Rename (Enter or leave the field to save), reorder, delete. All can be undone with "Undo last data edit"
scope.deleteSay: Deletes only this preset. Samples and tags aren't touched. Can be undone.
scope.exprTitle: Tag expression for the scope row
scope.exprSay: Tag conditions only, separate from the find bar's expression, and saved with the filter. Good for long-term scopes like "exclude all multi-speaker lines".
scope.exprHelp: NOT > AND > OR, parentheses, double quotes. "namespace:*" matches any tag in that namespace
batch.addSay: Adds local tags to the selected samples. Change inherited tags at their origin.
batch.removeSay: Only local tags can be removed (check them). Inherited tags show their origin; change them there.
batch.editSay: Empty = keep as is. Preview changes (before and after per field, nothing written) → apply (atomic) → undoable.
batch.previewSay: Will change {n} samples ({k} unchanged, skipped). If anything changes elsewhere before you apply, the whole batch is rejected and needs a new preview.
batch.noTags: The selected samples have no tags.
batch.field.name: Name
tags.manageSub: All tags in use, by facet. Right-click or use the buttons on the right to rename or remove globally (preview → apply → undoable).
tags.noGlobalAdd: Global add isn't allowed. To tag a batch of samples, check them and use "Add tags…", or draw a range tag on a source.
tags.report: Affects: {samples} samples with the local tag · {rangeTags} range tags · {sources} sources · speakers on {segments} lines
tags.speakerNote: (Speaker is a property of the line. This changes the name, so solo and multi-speaker tags change together, and the line is marked "speaker edited")
tags.folderSources: {n} sources in the sources folder aren't changed. Their work follows the folder; use "Work settings…" on the Sources page to rename the folder.
tags.derived: On {n} samples this tag is derived from a line's multiple speakers and can't be changed here (change the line's speakers).
tags.undoable: One edit, undoable with "Undo last data edit".
reason.same-tag: New name is the same as the old name
reason.person-rename-namespace: Person tags can only be renamed to person tags (character: / participants:)
reason.source-rename-namespace: Work / type tags can only be changed to the same kind
tag.goSource.segment: Go to origin (range tag / line on the Sources page)
tag.goSource.source: Go to origin (the source's work / type)
info.notePlaceholder: Note (saved when you leave the field)
info.chainBroken: (earlier origin was deleted with its source)
dock.exportDrag: Drag a file name to drop that file into a DAW or Finder
spectrum.head: Spectrum close-up (view within 30 s; computed from the selected audio, fixed −90–0 dB)
timeline.spectrumZoom: Spectrum shows {max} s or less: zoom in on a selection or scroll to zoom
visual.title: Picture binding
visual.subSample: Sample "{name}": its own binding overrides the source's picture
visual.subSource: Default picture for source "{name}": all its samples use this (except those with their own binding)
visual.none: No picture now (the source has no video stream and no binding)
visual.state.changed: Picture file changed: bind it again
visual.rules: Sync: picture time = sample's mapped source time + offset. Loop: sample's local time modulo animation length. Image: always this one. Audio is the master clock; the picture is muted.
visual.matchSub: Looks in each source's folder for a video / animation / image with the same name (ignoring extension). If several match, takes the first by video > animation > image. One edit, undoable.
video.title: Export video clip
video.say: H.264 MP4 + AAC (switch to a high-quality intermediate codec in Settings), with the sound of the matching version. Takes the nearest source frame by the mapping, no frame interpolation. Anything past the video stream is filled with black frames and flagged.
video.reused: This video clip was already exported; using the existing file
video.doneBlack: Exported video clip: {name} ({n} frames past the video stream filled with black)
reimport.title: Re-import
reimport.say: End comes from the file's length (a selected end is ignored). Can't be saved if it runs past the asset. The file is copied into the library folder in its original format, with no added silence, trimming, or speed change.
reimport.pickHint: Processed audio file (sample rate may differ from the original)
reimport.preview: File length {d} s · {rate} kHz · re-import end {end} s (in range; source {src})
reimport.outOfBounds: File length {d} s · re-import end {end} s: past the current asset ({max} s), can't be saved
reimport.name: Name
indep.title: Make {n} samples independent
indep.say: Saves the sound the samples use as lossless WAV slices and the picture as video clips (in Independent/ in the library folder). After that, even if the source is deleted, these samples can still play, export, and read their speech analysis. They just can't "return to source" for context.
indep.queuedDelete: Queued: make {n} samples independent, then delete the source (it stays as "media released")
indep.pickTitle: First make the samples to keep independent (optional)
indep.pickSay: Sound is saved as lossless slices and picture as video clips. The source record stays as "media released" and tag inheritance works as usual. You can no longer return to the source for context.
indep.size: {n} selected · about {mb} MB · {v} need picture clips
indep.none: None checked = all this source's samples are deleted (except independent ones)
indep.releaseNote: {n} samples that are (or will be) independent are kept. The source record becomes "media released" and stays in its work group; text layer and tags stay as usual
indep.deleteReleased: {n} media-released sources: delete along with their kept independent samples
indep.noBack: Source media released: independent samples can't return to the source for context
indep.viewerSay: The source file was deleted (only the reference; the file on disk wasn't touched). The work, text layer lines, SFX hints, range tags, OP/ED, and {n} independent samples are kept; their tag inheritance and origin work as usual.
relocate.title: Relocate {n} sources
relocate.say: Looks in "{folder}": first by path relative to the import root folder, then by file name (only if exactly one file has that name). Only the file location changes; existing assets, timing, analysis, and samples stay as they are.
relocate.doneChanged: Relocated {n} sources; {c} have different audio/video streams than before, please check
relocate.how.name: By file name
relocate.how.ambiguous: Several files with this name, none picked
relocate.how.in-root: In the sources folder: use "Change location…" in Settings
agent.undoBody: Undoes this session's {n} edits, newest first. If you or another session changed something afterward, it stops there and tells you. New samples, separated tracks, and exported files aren't in the edit history and won't be undone.
agent.undoneBlocked: Undid {n} edits. "{label}" was changed again afterward, so it stopped there ({remaining} left)
agent.confirmTitle: An agent wants to run an action that can't be undone
agent.confirmCountdown: No answer in {s} s counts as denied. Cancel or Esc to deny
agent.confirmWaiting: Waiting for your answer. Cancel or Esc to deny
agent.method.samples.independ: Make samples independent, then delete source
agent.preview.sourceDelete: {path}: will delete {samples} samples, {segments} lines, {hints} SFX hints, {rangeTags} range tags ({independent} independent samples kept)
agent.preview.independ: Will make {n} samples independent, then delete the source
agent.reasked: Data changed after asking, so nothing was run. Please confirm again with the new impact
history.title: History
history.missedReason.timeout: No answer for 2 minutes, not run
history.missedReason.closed: The agent disconnected before an answer, not run
reason.is-undo: This entry is itself an undo
reason.before-barrier: Before the point past which undo isn't possible
reason.changed-later: What it changed was changed again later
